title: Result-driven adaptive HTTP
question: For a new route, how does the engine choose between HTTP, the browser and a discovered API without false successes and at the lowest cost over subsequent runs (architecture §5.3)?

options.description: Always the browser, with the page stabilized (quiet network, scrolling and "load more" until stable)

First pass over a route: HTTP and browser on the first page; HTTP is kept if it yields the same records and links; declared total checked at the end of the route, otherwise the route is relearned in the browser
Like sampled-contract; if the browser is required, an API replay plan inferred from the sample's JSON traffic (page parameter or cursor chain), validated against the browser before use
HTTP, then the browser if the HTTP page contains no records

evidence.note: six renderings, five policies; quiet Mac

notes: A recurring job: what a route has learned is reused in subsequent runs, with the declared total as the invalidation event. The gate covers all variants of an option: a single page where it returns a wrong result blocks it.
